pratt-precollege-summer-2027.about:
Pratt PreCollege lets high-school students experience art-school life at Pratt Institute, one of the leading US schools of art, design and architecture. The four-week PreCollege Intensive offers university-level studio courses in art, design and architecture, with students living on Pratt's Brooklyn campus in Stabile or Pantas Hall; the two-week Explore programme is shorter and lighter, and an Online Summer Program serves grades 9–12.

For Summer 2027, residential programmes accept students aged 15.5–18 (those turning 16 by 31 December 2027 qualify). International students are welcome: Pratt issues an I-20 for an F-1 visa for the Intensive, Explore students may come on a tourist visa, and English proficiency is required (TOEFL iBT 76, IELTS 6, Duolingo 95 or PTE 48, or a year at an English-medium school). A limited number of full-ride Intensive scholarships exist for students with high artistic promise and significant need (typically household income USD 60,000 or less).
highlights: Studio courses at a leading art and design school
I-20 visa support for international Intensive students
Full-ride scholarships for high-need students
pratt-precollege-summer-2027.eligibility: Students aged 15.5–18 (16 by 31 Dec 2027). International students need English proficiency (TOEFL iBT 76 / IELTS 6 / Duolingo 95 / PTE 48 or equivalent schooling); Intensive requires an F-1 visa.
how_to_apply: Check 2027 courses and dates on the Pratt PreCollege site
Apply online and follow the course-specific requirements
International applicants: submit English proficiency and request an I-20 for the Intensive
Apply for the full-ride scholarship if eligible
Book housing and arrange your visa
pratt-precollege-summer-2027.costs: Paid; 2027 tuition and housing to be published (contact precollege@pratt.edu). Limited full-ride scholarships for the Intensive cover tuition, fees, housing and meals.

rcimun-2027.about:
RCIMUN is a student-led, THIMUN-affiliated Model United Nations conference held each year at Robert College in Istanbul. The 19th session in March 2026 brought together delegates from over 30 schools; the 2027 session has been announced with the theme "Promoting Altruism in an Increasingly Unstable World", and its Form 1, agenda items and special committees are already published.

The conference follows THIMUN rules of procedure with General Assembly committees, specialised agencies and special committees. Schools register delegations, and individual applications are also accepted. It is one of the most respected school MUNs in the region and a natural step for students from the Caucasus who want THIMUN-standard experience.
highlights: THIMUN-affiliated, run by Robert College students
2027 theme, agenda and Form 1 already published
Both school delegations and individual delegates
rcimun-2027.eligibility: High school students (typically ages 14-18) from any country, through a school delegation or an individual application. English is the working language.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 theme letter and agenda items on rcimun.org.
Ask your school MUN advisor to submit School Registration (Form 1), or use Individual Applications.
Receive country and committee allocations and prepare position papers.
Pay fees and arrange travel; see the Hotels and Logistics pages.
rcimun-2027.costs: Delegation and delegate fees are set by RCIMUN for the 2027 session; travel and accommodation paid by participants.

risd-pre-college-2027.about:
RISD Pre-College gives high-school students a taste of art-school life at one of the world's leading art and design schools. On campus, students choose a major studio (such as illustration, graphic design, architecture, fashion, film/animation or painting), take foundation drawing and art history, live in RISD residence halls and finish with a final exhibition. An online version runs at the same time for students who cannot travel.

In 2027 the on-campus programme runs 26 June–31 July (classes 28 June–30 July) and the online programme 21 June–29 July. Both are for rising high-school juniors and seniors; the online programme is explicitly open to students anywhere in the world. Applications open 4 November 2026 and 2027 costs are announced in November (2026: USD 12,495 residential, USD 9,595 commuter, USD 60 application fee).
highlights: Studio majors taught by RISD faculty
Final exhibition and portfolio development
Online option open worldwide
risd-pre-college-2027.eligibility: Rising high-school juniors and seniors. The online programme is open to students anywhere in the world; international students attending on campus need a US visa (contact RISD Pre-College for details).
how_to_apply: Pick on-campus or online and choose a major studio
Submit the online application from 4 November 2026 (USD 60 fee)
Pay the deposit within two business days of acceptance
Pay the balance by the date given in your offer (mid-March in 2026)
risd-pre-college-2027.costs: 2027 costs to be announced in November 2026. 2026: residential USD 12,495, commuter USD 9,595; plus art supplies (USD 800–1,000), laptop and travel. International payments via Flywire.

ritsumeikan-business-management-program-.about:
The Ritsumeikan Business Management Program (RBMP) is a two-week winter programme at the Osaka Ibaraki campus. Eight English-taught lectures cover Japanese Economy & Business, Strategic Management, Organisation & HRM and emerging topics.

Planned activities include a tea ceremony, a company visit, Microsoft Base Ritsumeikan, the Cup Noodles Museum and a buddy lunch with Ritsumeikan students. Up to 40 participants receive a completion certificate (no credit).

Open to undergraduate and graduate students enrolled at a university; high-school students are not eligible. Apply 2–25 November 2026; do not pay when applying.
highlights: English-taught lectures on Japanese business
Company and museum visits around Osaka
Small cohort of up to 40
ritsumeikan-business-management-program-.eligibility: Undergraduate or graduate students enrolled throughout the programme; English sufficient for lectures; no Japanese required; full attendance.
how_to_apply: Read the RBMP Application Guidelines PDF.
Apply between 2 and 25 November 2026.
Receive payment instructions on 1 December 2026.
Pay by 10 December 2026 and arrange travel.
ritsumeikan-business-management-program-.costs: Programme fee JPY 200,000 (lectures, activities, orientation); accommodation, meals and flights not included. No scholarships mentioned.

ritsumeikan-rwjp-express-february-2027.about:
RWJP Express is a compact winter programme at Ritsumeikan University's Kinugasa campus in Kyoto. Participants take three 50-minute Japanese classes a day for nine days, four Japan Studies activities, and group-based buddy exchanges with Ritsumeikan students through classes and cultural activities.

The February 2027 run is 16–26 February 2027. A completion certificate and instructor comments are issued (no credit). Optional housing is available at International House Taishogun.

It suits university students who want a short, intensive taste of Japanese language and life in Kyoto. Applications run 4–18 November 2026 and include a short handwritten essay in Japanese.
highlights: Daily Japanese classes in Kyoto
Buddy exchange with Ritsumeikan students
Optional international-house accommodation
ritsumeikan-rwjp-express-february-2027.eligibility: Enrolled university students (transcript and enrolment certificate required); JLPT N1 holders are not eligible; kana must be learned before arrival.
how_to_apply: Download the Application Kit PDF.
Submit applicant information between 4 and 18 November 2026.
Upload documents (Japanese essay, transcript, enrolment certificate, passport) via the link sent to you.
Pay fees and apply for a short-term stay visa if needed.
ritsumeikan-rwjp-express-february-2027.costs: Programme fee JPY 170,000 (incl. application fee); optional International House Taishogun JPY 42,500. Accommodation otherwise not included. No scholarships listed.

rwth-aachen-summer-schools-2027.about:
RWTH International Academy runs a series of two-week summer schools on the RWTH Aachen campus for international engineering and science students. 2027 courses include Artificial Intelligence in Industrial Applications (20 June – 3 July), Robot Operating Systems Essentials (20 June – 3 July, robot included), Sustainable Buildings & Green Cities (4–17 July), Automation and Simulation, Innovative Technologies in Automotive Engineering, Production Technology meets Industry 4.0, and Robotics and Innovation for Future Industries. Each two-week course gives 3 ECTS (about 75 hours of study).

Fees (EUR 2,490–2,990 for two weeks) include accommodation, catering and a transport ticket. There is a 10% early-bird discount (apply by 20 February, pay by 1 March 2027) and 50% Country Scholarships for students enrolled in listed countries (2027 list includes Türkiye, Egypt, South Korea, Malaysia, Indonesia, Brazil, Mexico and others, but not Georgia or Qatar), with a 1 April 2027 deadline.
highlights: Hands-on engineering topics: AI, robotics, sustainable cities, automotive
Accommodation, catering and transport included in the fee
Early-bird discount and 50% country scholarships
rwth-aachen-summer-schools-2027.eligibility: University students in engineering, science or related fields (see each course's requirements); good English. Country Scholarships only for students enrolled at universities in the listed countries (Georgia and Qatar not listed for 2027).
how_to_apply: Choose a 2027 summer school on the RWTH International Academy site and download its info package
Apply online (by 20 February 2027 for the early-bird discount)
If eligible, apply for the Country Scholarship by 1 April 2027
Pay the fee and arrange a visa if needed
rwth-aachen-summer-schools-2027.costs: EUR 2,490 (most courses) to EUR 2,990 (ROS, robot included) for two weeks, including accommodation, catering and transport ticket; 10% early-bird discount; 50% Country Scholarship (e.g. EUR 1,245–1,495) for eligible countries.

safespace-hacks-2026.about:
SafeSpace Hacks invites builders to turn an everyday moment of uncertainty (a suspicious message, confusing privacy settings, an emergency checklist, a community report) into a safer experience. Cybersecurity, privacy, scam awareness, safer communities, emergency readiness, trustworthy information and accessible safety tools all fit.

Apps, websites, games, hardware, AI tools and low-code projects are welcome, and you do not need to be a security specialist. Submissions close on 22 November 2026, with small cash prizes.
highlights: Broad safety/security theme
Any format: app, game, hardware, low-code
Beginner-friendly, small cash prizes
safespace-hacks-2026.eligibility: Open to participants worldwide who meet the Devpost rules (check minimum age on the Rules tab).
how_to_apply: Register on the official Devpost page
Join the organisers' Discord/discussion board to find teammates
Build your project during the hacking period
Submit code, demo video and description before the deadline

sans-holiday-hack-challenge-2026.about:
The Holiday Hack Challenge is SANS Institute's annual free cybersecurity event. Players explore a game world and solve hands-on challenges (terminals, web, forensics, cloud, AI security) at beginner to expert difficulty, then submit a report describing their solutions; standout entries win prizes.

The 2026 edition, 'The Pyramid on the Ice', opens in December and runs online over the holiday period. It is one of the most beginner-friendly ways to try practical cybersecurity, with hints and talks built into the game.
highlights: Completely free, play from anywhere
Challenges from beginner to expert level
Prizes for top reports
sans-holiday-hack-challenge-2026.eligibility: Open to anyone with an internet connection; prize eligibility follows the official rules. School students can play (with parental consent where needed).
how_to_apply: Open the official SANS Holiday Hack page
Click 'Alert Me When Game Opens' to be notified
Create a free account when the game launches in December
Solve challenges and submit your report before the deadline

science-without-borders-challenge-2027.about:
The Science Without Borders Challenge is an annual international art contest run by the Khaled bin Sultan Living Oceans Foundation to teach students about ocean science and conservation. The 2027 theme, 'Navigate with Care' (sponsored by the International Foundation for Aids to Navigation), asks students to show how mariners can protect both people and marine life by navigating safely and responsibly.

It is free and open to primary and secondary students aged 11–19 worldwide, judged in age groups. Winners receive scholarships of up to USD 500, and there is also a People's Choice award. New this year: entrants upload two photos of themselves creating the artwork, to confirm it is original and not AI-generated.
highlights: Free, for ages 11–19 anywhere
Scholarships up to USD 500
Combines art with ocean science
science-without-borders-challenge-2027.eligibility: Primary and secondary school students aged 11–19 from any country.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 theme and rules on the official page
Create an original 2D artwork on 'Navigate with Care'
Fill in the online entry form and upload a photo of the artwork
Upload two in-progress photos of yourself creating it, before 1 March 2027

sciences-po-virtual-undergraduate-open-h.about:
Sciences Po's Virtual Undergraduate Open House Day lets prospective students discover the undergraduate College (its multidisciplinary Bachelor's in social sciences and humanities, its regional campuses and dual-degree options) without travelling to France.

The event runs on 28 November 2026 from 9 am to 4 pm on a dedicated platform with Zoom sessions, in English and French so international applicants can follow. Registration is free; all access information is sent by email after you sign up.
highlights: Bilingual English/French sessions
Learn about campuses and dual degrees
Free, from anywhere
sciences-po-virtual-undergraduate-open-h.eligibility: Anyone considering undergraduate study at Sciences Po, from any country.
how_to_apply: Open the registration page
Fill in the sign-up form
Receive event details by email
Join the sessions on 28 Nov 2026

season-of-kde-2027.about:
Season of KDE (SoK) has run every year since 2013. It is similar to, but less formal than, Google Summer of Code: anyone can propose a code or non-code project (documentation, translation, design, promotion) from KDE's ideas list, or suggest their own idea after finding a mentor through KDE's mailing lists and Matrix channels.

The 2027 season is expected to follow the usual timeline: opening in mid-December, contributor applications closing in mid-January, about ten weeks of mentored work from late January to March, and certificates for successful contributors. It is free and a respected stepping stone towards GSoC and open-source careers.
highlights: Mentored open-source project
Code and non-code projects
Certificate for successful contributors
season-of-kde-2027.eligibility: Open to everyone (students especially welcome) from any country; good English for communicating with mentors.
how_to_apply: Read the ideas page for the 2027 season
Contact a mentor and start contributing early
Submit your proposal before the application deadline (mid-January)
Work on your project with your mentor from late January

sfs-amazonian-plant-biodiversity-and-tra.about:
The School for Field Studies (SFS) runs field-based environmental study-abroad programmes at its own research centres around the world. This summer course, SFS 3832 Amazonian Plant Biodiversity and Traditional Medicine, is based in the Upper Amazon of Peru, with field sites including the Takiwasi Center in Tarapoto. Students attend lectures by resident faculty, carry out field exercises and a directed research component, and earn 4 university credits on an accredited transcript.

The 2027 programme runs 31 May to 29 June 2027. Summer programmes require applicants to be 18+ by the start date with a GPA of about 2.6 or higher and no science prerequisite; admission is rolling with no application fee, and the listed summer deadline is 1 April. SFS offers need-based scholarships; 2027 programme cost is 'coming soon'. Applicants from universities outside the US should confirm credit transfer and eligibility with SFS admissions.
highlights: Four weeks living at an SFS field station
4 accredited university credits
Rolling admission, no application fee, need-based scholarships
sfs-amazonian-plant-biodiversity-and-tra.eligibility: University students aged 18+ by programme start, GPA about 2.6+ (holistic review), no prerequisites. A transcript and home-university approval are requested; students from non-US universities should confirm with admissions@fieldstudies.org.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page and SFS admissions requirements
Submit the free online application with your university transcript
Apply early (rolling; listed deadline 1 April)
Apply for SFS need-based scholarships
Arrange visa, vaccinations and flights once accepted
sfs-amazonian-plant-biodiversity-and-tra.costs: Programme fee for 2027 'coming soon' on the SFS page (covers tuition, room, board and field trips); airfare extra. Need-based SFS scholarships available.

sfs-wildlife-health-and-conservation-sum.about:
The School for Field Studies (SFS) runs field-based environmental study-abroad programmes at its own research centres around the world. This summer course, SFS 3254 Wildlife Health and Conservation, is based in Kimana in the Amboseli landscape, with fieldwork on Amboseli grazing lands, at a cattle dip and market, and an expedition to the Maasai Mara. Students attend lectures by resident faculty, carry out field exercises and a directed research component, and earn 4 university credits on an accredited transcript.

The 2027 programme runs 5 July to 3 August 2027. Summer programmes require applicants to be 18+ by the start date with a GPA of about 2.6 or higher and no science prerequisite; admission is rolling with no application fee, and the listed summer deadline is 1 May. SFS offers need-based scholarships; 2027 programme cost is 'coming soon'. Applicants from universities outside the US should confirm credit transfer and eligibility with SFS admissions.
highlights: Four weeks living at an SFS field station
4 accredited university credits
Rolling admission, no application fee, need-based scholarships

sit-kenya-public-health-tropics-internsh.about:
SIT's Public Health in the Tropics Internship is based in Kisumu on Lake Victoria. Students complete an internship (4 credits) at a health organisation such as the Kisumu County Department of Health, Jaramogi Oginga Odinga Teaching and Referral Hospital or Nyanza Reproductive Health Society, arranged with SIT's help, plus a 3-credit seminar on public-health planning and delivery in tropical countries, Kenya's social and political history and the social determinants of health.

The programme covers prevention and management of malaria, HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis, includes a weekend excursion to the Maasai Mara, and introduces Kiswahili; teaching is in English. It runs 1 June–19 July 2027 with an application deadline of 1 April 2027 (places are filling). No prerequisites, though a background in health or policy studies is preferred.

Maasai Mara excursion and Kiswahili introduction

sit-madagascar-traditional-medicine-summ.about:
This SIT programme examines how traditional and biomedical healthcare coexist in Madagascar. Students study Madagascar's healthcare models and delivery, health beliefs and religious practices, postcolonial politics of healthcare access, and ethnobotany and folk remedies (4 credits), and take introductory Malagasy (2 credits). Teaching is in English; students with French can use it.

The programme is based in Antananarivo with homestays, ten days in Andasibe and excursions to the west coast (Morondava) and central regions. It runs 15 June–28 July 2027; apply by 1 April 2027 (places filling). SIT advertises up to USD 1,250 in flight credits for new programmes.
highlights: Homestays and ten days in the Andasibe rainforest area
Ethnobotany and traditional healers
6 university credits, taught in English

sit-panama-marine-ecology-blue-carbon-su.about:
Based in Panama City, this SIT programme studies marine biodiversity on both the Pacific and Caribbean coasts and the links between mangroves, seagrass meadows and coral reefs, including their role in storing 'blue carbon' and slowing climate change. Students learn field methods for measuring carbon and biodiversity, work at Bocas del Toro, Coiba Island and Guna Yala, and complete an independent field project (two 3-credit courses).

It runs 1 June–13 July 2027; apply by 1 April 2027 (places filling). Prior coursework in environmental studies, ecology or biology is required and students must swim well, since most time is spent in the water. Teaching is in English; SIT summer scholarships generally range from USD 500 to 3,000.
highlights: Pacific and Caribbean field sites incl. Coiba Island
Blue-carbon and reef field methods
Independent marine research project

sit-south-africa-diplomacy-internship-su.about:
This SIT programme combines a five-week internship (5 credits) with an organisation working on diplomacy, politics or international relations and a 3-credit seminar. Topics include South Africa's transition from apartheid to democracy, its foreign policy, the African Union and BRICS, regional security and South–South relations, plus career paths in diplomacy.

The programme is based in Durban with excursions to Johannesburg, Maputo (Mozambique) and Cape Town. It runs 1 June–23 July 2027; apply by 1 April 2027 (places filling). No prerequisites; teaching is in English.

Study the African Union and BRICS from Africa
Excursions to Johannesburg, Maputo and Cape Town

skku-wise-winter-2026-27.about:
WISE is the winter programme of Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU), one of Korea's leading universities with roots going back to 1398. Classes run 22 December 2026 – 8 January 2027 in Seoul, with English-taught courses, group cultural activities and field trips included in tuition.

Students taking two courses can add an optional research internship in an SKKU lab (placement assisted, not guaranteed). Dormitory housing is optional.

Registration closes 13 December 2026. Groups of 3+ students from the same university get 30% off; WISE/ISS alumni get 40% off.
highlights: Optional research internship in SKKU labs
Cultural activities and field trips included
30% group discount
skku-wise-winter-2026-27.eligibility: University students worldwide (see WISE policies page).

Register online by 13 December 2026.
Pay tuition and the 100,000 KRW registration fee.
Book the optional dormitory.
skku-wise-winter-2026-27.costs: Registration 100,000 KRW; tuition 1,760,000 KRW (1 course), 3,080,000 KRW (2 courses), 3,740,000 KRW (2 courses + internship); dorm 690,000 KRW. Discounts: 30% groups of 3+, 40% alumni.

slovene-summer-school-ljubljana-2027.about:
The Summer School of Slovene Language is run by the Centre for Slovene as a Second and Foreign Language at the University of Ljubljana's Faculty of Arts. From 5 to 16 July 2027 participants take a morning course (four 45-minute lessons a day, Monday–Friday) at their level, can add an afternoon conversation elective, and join an accompanying programme of lectures, workshops, cultural events and sport about three times a week. The course is worth 60–80 class hours (3–4 ECTS).

Anyone interested in learning Slovene can register. The Jana Zemljarič Miklavčič Scholarship Trust funds a few places (including two grants for the two-week summer school) for candidates without Slovene background who are actively engaged in Slovene culture or promote Slovenia; members of Slovene minorities abroad and descendants of emigrants can apply for ministry scholarships covering tuition.
highlights: Intensive Slovene at all levels, 3–4 ECTS
Lectures, workshops, cultural and sports programme in Ljubljana
Scholarship trust grants for non-Slovene promoters of Slovene culture
slovene-summer-school-ljubljana-2027.eligibility: Adults who want to learn Slovene; all nationalities. Jana Zemljarič Miklavčič grants: people without Slovene background who are active in Slovene culture or promote Slovenia. Ministry scholarships: members of Slovene minorities abroad and descendants of Slovene emigrants.
how_to_apply: Fill in the Summer School application form on centerslo.si
For the Jana Zemljarič Miklavčič grant, email your application by 1 May 2027
For the diaspora scholarship, use the online scholarship form by 15 May 2027
Pay the tuition (if not on a scholarship) and arrange accommodation and travel
slovene-summer-school-ljubljana-2027.costs: EUR 785 for the two-week morning course and EUR 240 for the afternoon elective; tuition covers learning materials and the accompanying programme. Accommodation and travel extra unless covered by a scholarship.

slovene-winter-school-ljubljana-2027.about:
The Winter School of Slovene Language is an intensive two-week course run by the University of Ljubljana's Centre for Slovene as a Second and Foreign Language, from 25 January to 5 February 2027. Participants follow a morning language course at their level (optional afternoon elective) and an accompanying programme of about 10 hours with lectures, workshops (for example a Kurent carnival-mask workshop), cultural events and sport, such as a guided visit to the National Museum of Contemporary History.

It suits anyone who wants to start or improve Slovene quickly, from complete beginners to advanced learners. Applications are made with the online form at least two weeks before the start.
highlights: Intensive Slovene at all levels in two weeks
Cultural accompanying programme in Ljubljana
Low fee compared with most European winter schools
slovene-winter-school-ljubljana-2027.eligibility: Adults of any nationality who want to learn Slovene; all levels.
how_to_apply: Fill in the Winter School application form on centerslo.si
Apply at least two weeks before 25 January 2027
Pay the tuition as instructed
Arrange travel and accommodation in Ljubljana
slovene-winter-school-ljubljana-2027.costs: EUR 620 for the morning course and accompanying programme; EUR 240 for the optional afternoon elective. Accommodation and travel extra.

smu-global-summer-programme-2027.about:
The SMU Global Summer Programme (GSP) brings university students from around the world to Singapore Management University's city-centre campus for four weeks. Courses run in three tracks: Asian Insights, Digital Intelligence and Sustainable Futures. Each course carries one SMU credit unit (36 contact hours) in seminar-style classes; you can take up to two courses in one session.

Session 1 runs 28 June – 23 July 2027 and Session 2 runs 12 July – 6 August 2027. Some courses are postgraduate-level and can earn exemptions in SMU master's programmes.

Applications are open from 8 January to 15 April 2027. Applicants need a transcript and, if not taught in English, IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 90.
highlights: Three tracks: Asian Insights, Digital Intelligence, Sustainable Futures
Seminar classes at a top Asian business university
Discounts for partner-university and group applicants
smu-global-summer-programme-2027.eligibility: Undergraduates, postgraduates and recent graduates worldwide; IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 90 if your university does not teach in English.
how_to_apply: Choose session and up to two courses.
Apply online between 8 January and 15 April 2027.
Pay the S$150 application fee within 3 days.
After acceptance pay the S$1,000 advance and apply for a Student's Pass if needed.
smu-global-summer-programme-2027.costs: Application S$150; tuition S$3,270 (one course) or S$5,450 (two); miscellaneous S$256.50. 10–15% discounts for partner/group students. Accommodation and living costs extra.

soliya-advanced-facilitation-training-sp.about:
Soliya's Advanced Facilitation Training is a 10-week live programme (also offered in a 5-week format) in which small, diverse cohorts work closely with Soliya trainers on Zoom, with asynchronous materials on Brightspace. Participants practise facilitation in real time, receive extensive individual feedback and build skills in active listening, handling difficult dynamics and group collaboration.

The spring 2027 round runs 15 March – 20 May 2027 (register by 24 February). Completion earns a Soliya certificate and is required for certification; certified facilitators can join Soliya's Community of Practice and become eligible for paid facilitation in its virtual exchange programmes.
highlights: Live practice in small international cohorts
Soliya certificate on completion
Route to paid facilitation work
soliya-advanced-facilitation-training-sp.eligibility: Adults (18+) from any country; completion of the introductory course or equivalent facilitation experience is expected.
how_to_apply: Complete the introductory course (or show prior facilitation experience)
Register for the spring round before 24 Feb 2027
Pay the training fee (bundles available)
Join the weekly live sessions from 15 Mar 2027
soliya-advanced-facilitation-training-sp.costs: Paid training (see price plans and bundles on the official page).

soliya-global-circles-2026-27.about:
Global Circles is Soliya's open-enrolment virtual exchange. Each round brings together hundreds of participants who are placed into small groups of about 15 people, balanced across countries, backgrounds and viewpoints, and each group is guided by a professional facilitator.

A round lasts two weeks (about 10 hours): two live 2.5-hour Zoom sessions plus short asynchronous prompts on Soliya's platform. The November 2026 round (9–21 Nov, live sessions 13 and 21 Nov) asks how AI is changing job markets. Rounds usually run in February, March, April, June, September, October and November.

Participants earn a certificate of participation and join Soliya's alumni network. It is a low-commitment way to practise cross-cultural dialogue, active listening and discussing contested topics with peers from many countries.
highlights: Small groups of ~15 from many countries, with a pro facilitator
Two live Zoom sessions plus light async work over two weeks
Certificate and alumni network; limited scholarships
soliya-global-circles-2026-27.eligibility: Anyone aged 18 or older (students or professionals) with internet access and conversational English. No nationality restrictions are stated.

Fill in the online application form (ask about a scholarship there if needed)
Pay the participation fee once accepted
Join the two live sessions and the online activities
soliya-global-circles-2026-27.costs: Participation fee USD 95 per round; a limited number of scholarships are available via the application form.

soliya-intro-online-dialogue-facilitatio.about:
Soliya's Introduction to Online Dialogue Facilitation is the first step of its facilitator pathway. Over five weeks (11 January – 15 February 2027) and about 12–15 hours, participants study the functions of dialogue and facilitation, online group management and a foundational facilitation toolbox, with weekly assignments, individual feedback on their own facilitation profile and two optional live sessions.

Graduates can continue to Soliya's Advanced Facilitation Training and practicum, which leads to certification and paid facilitation opportunities in Soliya's virtual exchange programmes. It suits university students interested in conflict resolution, education, international relations or community work.
highlights: Self-paced, with weekly deadlines
Individual feedback on your facilitation style
Pathway to certification and paid facilitation work
soliya-intro-online-dialogue-facilitatio.eligibility: Adults (18+) from any country with good English. (A separate Arabic course, Virtu-PEACE, is limited to residents of certain countries.)

Register for the English course before 8 Jan 2027
Pay the training fee (bundle discounts available)
Complete the weekly modules from 11 Jan 2027
soliya-intro-online-dialogue-facilitatio.costs: Training fee USD 450; bundle discounts for multiple trainings.

spacie-climate-change-summer-school-2027.about:
The Climate Change Summer School, launched by SpaCIE in 2021, holds its 7th edition on the Cantoblanco campus of Universidad Autónoma de Madrid from 12 to 23 July 2027. Professors from economics, law, biology and political science teach a multidisciplinary, English-taught course on the science, economics and policy of climate change (6 ECTS).

A 4-week track (28 June – 23 July, 12 ECTS) adds UAM's 'Environmental Economics and Policy Analysis' course.

It suits university students from any discipline who care about climate action. See the official costs page and brochure for fees.
highlights: Multidisciplinary: economics, law, biology, politics
6 or 12 ECTS
Combine with UAM's economics summer school
spacie-climate-change-summer-school-2027.eligibility: University students from any field (see the official how-to-apply page).

Apply via the official 'how to apply' page.
Pay the programme fee after admission.
Arrange accommodation in Madrid.
spacie-climate-change-summer-school-2027.costs: Fees on the official costs page.

st-andrews-summer-academic-experience-20.about:
The Summer Academic Experience Courses (SAEC) are the only international summer programmes at the University of St Andrews for high-school students. From 24 July to 14 August 2027, students aged 16–18 live in a university hall and take a university-style course in subjects such as Management, Economics and Entrepreneurship; Creative Writing; Sustainable Development; Cinema, Ideas and Society; and Diverse Intelligences, ending with projects such as business pitches, plus evening and weekend activities and trips.

The all-inclusive fee is GBP 6,950. Three full scholarships (tuition, accommodation and trips) are available for the Diverse Intelligences course and 10% partial scholarships (GBP 695) for Creative Writing, Sustainable Development and Cinema, Ideas and Society; scholarship applicants must show both academic merit and financial need, with a 500-word statement, by 25 February 2027.
highlights: Residential university experience at St Andrews for 16–18s
Small-group academic courses with projects and trips
Three full need-and-merit scholarships plus partial awards
st-andrews-summer-academic-experience-20.eligibility: Students aged 16–18 on arrival with English at about CEFR B2 or above. All nationalities (visa may be required).

Pay the GBP 500 deposit within 14 days of an unconditional offer
Pay the remaining GBP 6,450 by 28 April 2027
st-andrews-summer-academic-experience-20.costs: All-inclusive fee GBP 6,950 for 2027 (see the page for exactly what it covers); travel extra. Scholarships: 3 full (Diverse Intelligences) and partial GBP 695 awards.

st-johns-cambridge-webinar-introduction-.about:
St John's College, one of the largest Cambridge colleges, runs a 2026–27 series of webinars for prospective undergraduates. In this session, the Assistant Undergraduate Admissions Tutor and Director of Studies in Mathematics, Dr Matthias Dörrzapf, explains how Cambridge works (the collegiate system, supervisions, courses) and how it fits into the wider higher-education landscape, then answers questions.

It takes place online on Monday 9 November 2026 from 5:00 to 6:15 pm UK time. It is useful for younger secondary-school students planning a future Cambridge application.
highlights: Led by a Cambridge admissions tutor
Live Q&A
Free, online
st-johns-cambridge-webinar-introduction-.eligibility: Prospective undergraduate applicants and their parents/teachers, from any country.
how_to_apply: Open the event page on the Cambridge undergraduate site
Book a place
Receive joining instructions
Attend on 9 Nov 2026 at 5 pm UK time

stanford-global-sustainability-challenge.about:
The Global Sustainability Challenge (GSC) is an annual Stanford University initiative, run with a collective of leading universities (including HKUST, IIT Bombay, TUM and UNESP), in which university students design, build and showcase real-world sustainability solutions. Season 1 drew 3,000+ students from 90+ countries. In 2026–27 there are two themes: Sustainable Energy (generation, storage, access, efficiency, microgrids) and Adaptation & Resilience (water, food and heat resilience).

Teams of 1–6 undergraduate, graduate or PhD students, from any discipline and any country (teams can mix universities and countries), move through three phases: Ignite (team up, research and design, until 22 November 2026), Build (prototype and test, December 2026 – 22 February 2027) and Shine (regional finals in February–March 2027 and a Global Finale in Hangzhou, China, on 20–21 May 2027). Mentors, workshops and judges' feedback are built in; the prize pool is USD 35,000+, and winners may join Stanford's EcoGlobal ecopreneurship programme.
highlights: Open to university students worldwide, teams of 1–6
Mentors, workshops and regional finals
USD 35,000+ prizes; finale in Hangzhou
stanford-global-sustainability-challenge.eligibility: Undergraduate, graduate and PhD students anywhere in the world, in teams of 1–6 (at least one member must be 18+ by 1 Jan 2027). All disciplines welcome.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the GSC hub ('Join the Challenge')
Form or join a team (up to 6) and pick a theme
Complete the Phase 1 deliverables by 22 Nov 2026
Build and test your solution and present at your regional final
stanford-global-sustainability-challenge.costs: Free to participate; travel to finals depends on the regional host and partner support.

stanford-math-tournament-online-2027.about:
The Stanford Math Tournament (SMT) is run entirely by Stanford students, with support from the Stanford Undergraduate Mathematics Organization and the Department of Mathematics, and had over 2,000 participants globally in 2025. The in-person contest on Stanford's campus is for around 800 US students.

To widen access, SMT also hosts an online tournament, similar to the in-person contest, shortly after the April event; it is open to all middle- and high-school students from anywhere in the world. Past problems are on the website and are excellent olympiad training.
highlights: Run by Stanford students
Open to students worldwide online
Past problems available for practice
stanford-math-tournament-online-2027.eligibility: Middle- and high-school students anywhere in the world.

Register for the online tournament when it opens
Practise with past SMT problems
Compete online on the tournament day
stanford-math-tournament-online-2027.costs: No fee is stated for the online tournament on the official site; check when registration opens.

stanford-pre-collegiate-summer-institute.about:
Stanford Pre-Collegiate Summer Institutes are intensive two-week online courses in a single subject (business, bioscience, computer science, creative writing, engineering, mathematics or philosophy), taught live in small classes so students can work with academically motivated peers from around the world without travelling.

The programme is for students in grades 8–11 and is non-credit enrichment. In 2026 there were two sessions (15–26 June and 6–17 July) with an application deadline of 13 March 2026; 2027 should follow a similar timeline. Because it is online, it is one of the most accessible ways for international students to take a Stanford-run course.
highlights: Live online classes from Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies
Seven subject areas from philosophy to engineering
No travel or visa needed
stanford-pre-collegiate-summer-institute.eligibility: Students in grades 8–11 from any country with good English; selection based on academic record and essays.
how_to_apply: Choose a subject and session when 2027 courses are posted
Complete the online application with essays and transcript
Apply before the mid-March deadline (13 Mar in 2026)
Check time zones: classes are live on Pacific time
stanford-pre-collegiate-summer-institute.costs: Paid online programme; tuition and financial aid details on the Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies website.

stanford-summer-humanities-institute-202.about:
The Stanford Summer Humanities Institute is a residential programme in which small groups of high-school students spend three weeks in an intensive seminar on a humanities topic (philosophy, history, literature, politics and similar) led by a Stanford professor, supported by graduate-student instructors. Students read primary texts, debate in seminar, write a research paper and live on the Stanford campus.

The programme is for rising high-school juniors and seniors (grades 10–11 at the time of application). In 2026 it ran in two sessions (21 June–10 July and 12–31 July) with an application deadline of 2 February 2026; the 2027 dates should follow a similar pattern. Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies describes its students as coming from the US and around the world.
highlights: Seminars led by Stanford professors
Write a university-style research paper
Live on the Stanford campus for three weeks
stanford-summer-humanities-institute-202.eligibility: Students in grades 10–11 at the time of application (rising juniors and seniors), from the US or abroad, with strong English and academic record.
how_to_apply: Watch the Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies site for 2027 seminar topics
Submit the online application with essays and transcript
Provide a teacher recommendation as requested
Apply before the early-February deadline (2 Feb in 2026)
Request financial aid within the application if needed
stanford-summer-humanities-institute-202.costs: Paid residential programme; tuition and need-based aid details on Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies pages.

stem2connect-ai-hackathon-2026.about:
The STEM2Connect AI Hackathon is a global, multi-week programme rather than a weekend sprint, putting learning and mentorship ahead of pressure. Students work alone or in teams of up to six to turn a focused idea into a working AI-powered project in one of five tracks: Education, Healthcare, Sustainability, Scientific Research or Community Impact.

Live sessions (all recorded) cover problem validation, AI tools and APIs, design and pitching, and mentors from industry, research and engineering help teams scope ideas and prepare for Demo Day. AI coding assistants are allowed with disclosure. Submissions close on 21 November 2026.
highlights: No coding experience needed
Recorded live sessions + industry mentors
Five impact tracks, teams up to 6
stem2connect-ai-hackathon-2026.eligibility: Students aged 13+ enrolled in middle school, high school, college or university, anywhere in the world.
how_to_apply: Register on the official Devpost page
Join the organisers' Discord/discussion board to find teammates
Build your project during the hacking period
Submit code, demo video and description before the deadline

suiss-edinburgh-2027.about:
The Scottish Universities' International Summer School, based at the University of Edinburgh, has run summer courses in literature and the arts for decades. In 2027 it runs from 12 July to 21 August with the Text and Context programme (Modernism, Contemporary Literature, Scottish Literature), a four-week Creative Writing course with author masterclasses, a Queer Studies course and a two-week Contemporary British and Irish Theatre and Performance course timed with the Edinburgh International Festival and Fringe. Teaching combines daily lectures by guest scholars with small seminars; credit is available for an extra fee.

SUISS offers full and partial scholarships funded by sponsors for applicants from specific countries, in specific subjects, or exceptional literature students who could not attend without help; awards are based on financial need, merit and likely contribution. Scholarship applicants apply on the regular form (page 4) with a supporting letter by 29 March 2027.
highlights: Courses timed with the Edinburgh festivals
Creative writing with acclaimed authors' masterclasses
Full and partial need-based scholarships
suiss-edinburgh-2027.eligibility: Students and others with strong English (one reference must certify your fluency and abilities as a student); courses are pitched at an advanced level. All nationalities; some scholarships are restricted to certain countries or subjects.
how_to_apply: Download the application form for your chosen course(s) from the SUISS application page
Include one academic or employer reference and, for scholarships, a letter explaining why you should be considered
Email the form to suiss@ed.ac.uk with a GBP 100 deposit (scholarship applicants exempt)
Scholarship deadline 29 March 2027; regular deadline 26 April 2027
suiss-edinburgh-2027.costs: Course fees (by length) e.g. Text & Context GBP 1,167 / 2,076 / 3,075; Creative Writing GBP 2,334–3,520; optional credit fee GBP 80–200; catered study-room accommodation GBP 864 (2 weeks) to GBP 2,880 (6 weeks). Fees include weekday lunches and a social programme. Scholarships cover fees fully or partly.

sussex-international-summer-school-2027.about:
The Sussex International Summer School offers undergraduate-level modules taught by Sussex faculty on the campus just outside Brighton on England's south coast. Session one runs 28 June – 16 July 2027 and session two 19 July – 6 August 2027; you can take one or both. A separate Physics stream runs four-week sessions (28 June – 23 July and 26 July – 20 August 2027).

It is open to current university students, graduates and students due to begin university in September 2027, so final-year high-school students with a confirmed place can join. You need a GPA of about 2.8/4 or equivalent and IELTS 6.0.

Modules carry academic credit, and the programme includes a social and excursion programme around Brighton and London.

syntax-summit-dsl-hackathon-2027.about:
Syntax Summit challenges participants to go beyond writing code and create a language: a domain-specific language (DSL) that makes problems in one field (AI, robotics, finance, healthcare, education, cybersecurity, games, IoT and more) more intuitive to express.

Submissions include a repository with the parser, interpreter, transpiler or compiler, documentation, sample programs and a demo video of up to 5 minutes. Solo entries and teams are both welcome. The window runs until 14 January 2027, and prizes (such as Best User Experience) are non-cash. A strong project for students interested in compilers and computer-science theory.
highlights: Build a real DSL, parser or compiler
Long window until 14 Jan 2027
Solo or team

tallinn-winter-school-2027.about:
Tallinn Winter School, run by Tallinn University since 2010, offers short courses in the Estonian capital from 11 to 29 January 2027. Options include Estonian and Russian language (3 weeks), Introduction to Estonia and Finno-Ugric Cultures, Academic Writing in English, Data Visualisation with Python and AI, Experimental Interaction Design, Design Systems with Figma and AI, Storytelling in Marketing, and world-politics courses on diplomacy, climate justice and emerging technologies.

Courses last one to three weeks and come with a cultural programme in Tallinn, a UNESCO-listed old town and a European tech hub. Prices range from €140 to €800 per course.

The Estonian Education and Youth Board funds free places (tuition plus a double room) on Estonian language courses for foreigners already learning Estonian. Registration is open until 1 December 2026.

Affordable courses from €140
Free places for learners of Estonian
